extracted.subtask_description: Classroom case-discussion prompt for analyzing a comedian's crisis response and the ethics/communication choices around embellishing stories in stand-up. Focuses on integrity, evidence, organization, tone, and reputational outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity / amount of embellishment
rubrics_metrics.description: How much is too much 'stretching the truth'?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students can discuss issues of integrity and analyze evidence in this situation. Consider differences in standards of integrity for comedians, politicians, organizational leaders, entrepreneurs, job applicants, etc. The page raises the question of whether embellishments with 'societal value' give a comedian greater moral standing than 'pointless' fabrications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis management strategy: respond vs. move on
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical crisis management dictates you should move on, not fixate, but entertainers may benefit from addressing controversy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh 'move on' advice against the attention economy and Rahm Emanuel's advice to 'never let a good crisis go to waste.' Minhaj 'split the difference'—he did not linger but dedicated a solid chunk of jokes and a response video, producing strong audience reaction. Discuss timing, fixation risk, and opportunity in choosing whether to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of supporting evidence and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between what really happened and what was changed; present supporting materials to substantiate claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minhaj showed headlines, played audio from the New Yorker interview, and addressed stories in detail. The article notes he 'does provide good evidence of the reporter ignoring or missing information.' Guidance: show corroborating materials (audio, clips, documents) and clearly separate fact from dramatized elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledging harm and apologizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Apologize to those hurt and address the impact of routines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minhaj apologized to those hurt by his routines and directly addressed three stories. Discuss the role of apology in crisis response and when a direct apology is necessary versus a defensive stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear organization and explicit main point up front
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclude with or present a main point clearly and early (direct organization plan—up front!).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece praises Minhaj for concluding with a main point about not 'faking racism.' Instructional note: present the primary claim/defense early so audiences understand the takeaway; avoid getting lost in minutiae.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing the severity and moral comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame the offense's severity and compare to other kinds of falsehoods to justify or contextualize embellishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minhaj contrasted his 'embellishments' with George Santos's lies, calling the latter 'pointless' and asserting his own stories have societal value. Guidance: framing can be used to argue moral standing, but beware minimizing serious harms (the article notes Minhaj's unfortunate comment invoking child abuse as an example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leveraging controversy to engage audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Use criticism or scandal strategically to generate audience engagement and potentially elevate reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minhaj dedicated part of his show to the controversy and a follow-up 21-minute video; the jokes and response 'got one of the biggest responses of the night' and a writer speculated the scandal 'might be the best thing that ever happened to him.' Discuss risk/benefit and ethics of using scandal as material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of fictionalization / 'emotional truth' labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Be explicit about the degree of fictionalization in stories (e.g., 'seed of truth' / 'seventy per cent emotional truth—. . . thirty per cent hyperbole').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minhaj described his style as built around a 'seed of truth' with a stated percentage of 'emotional truth' vs hyperbole. Guidance: consider whether disclosing that stories are embellished helps manage expectations and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of medium and presentation methods for response
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the medium (live show, video, press statement) and tactics (showing clips/audio) that best demonstrate your evidence and reach audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minhaj used a Beacon Theater set piece and a 21-minute video that showed headlines and clips and played audio. The article also references a Slate deep-dive and New Yorker reporting; guidance: pick formats that allow transparent presentation of supporting materials and reach intended stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing reputational consequences and outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the response will avoid cancellation, repair harm, or possibly elevate reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article suggests Minhaj's approach 'may have avoided his getting "cancelled" and might even elevate his reputation.' Guidance: analyze likely reputational trajectories, short-term attention versus long-term trust, and whether the defense sustains credibility.
